verdict.reasoning: Patient reports feeling unwell for four days with sore throat and runny nose progressing to cough and fatigue: "I've been feeling kind of under the weather for the past four days"; "it started with the sore throat and runny nose... it's sort of going into a cough now"; "kind of bad and tired." The cough is described as constant: "it's sort of there, all the time."

Patient attributes illness onset to a coworker who was sneezing and whose kids were sick: "this colleague of mine, she just kept sneezing next to me, all the time. I think her kids are catching something from their kindergarten."

Sore throat was painful with swallowing for one or two days and is now improving: "it started as normal sore throat, and was quite painful for a couple days, but then it was past" and "it was quite painful to swallow, for one or two days" and later "the sort throat is kind of going away."

Patient describes current nasal symptoms as congestion rather than clear discharge: "Yeah yeah, it's uh it's clearing up" and then "Sort of getting my nose stuffed all the time. It's very hard to get it free." The doctor asked if discharge was clear or colored, but the patient did not state that the discharge was clear; only congestion is confirmed.
Onset and nature of cough: "yeah that started recently, like just maybe yesterday. And it's dry for now... it's sort of there, all the time."
Patient explicitly mentions night sweats: "I forgot to mention, that I'm also having night sweats."
Initial fever relieved by paracetamol or ibuprofen: "I had some fever in the beginning, but it's now sort of going down. I've been taking some Paracetamol and Ibuprofen for that, and they help."

Intermittent generalized headaches: "any headaches at all?" Patient: "yeah, yeah. That's still there." Location and pattern: "it's sort of general... they're not always there, but you know every now and then they will come and go."
Muscle pains for past couple of days: "any general muscle pain or aches, joint pain?" Patient: "Yeah, yeah. Yeah that's, that sort of started in the past couple days."

Shortness of breath on exertion only and no chest pain: "no pain in chest, but I noticed that I feel a bit winded on exertion"; clarified by doctor: "do you feel more short of breath would you say, on exertion?... and that's mainly on exercise. But when you're resting, there's no problem." Patient agrees: "Yeah, yeah. When I'm resting it's OK."

Denies nausea/vomiting and reports normal bowels and urine: "any feeling nausea or any vomiting?" Patient: "No, none of that."; "Tell me about your bowels. Are your bowels working OK?" Patient: "yeah, yeah. Think so."; "You're passing urine OK?" Patient: "Yeah, yeah."

Decreased appetite and increased fluid intake: "How's your appetite, sir?" Patient: "Yeah I've been, I've been drinking a lot more than the usual" and later "maybe a bit less than what I would usually have" referring to food intake.

No rash, ear symptoms, or visual changes: Ear: "Any pain in, in your ears at all?" Patient: "no" and "No, I don't think so" for blockage/discharge; Vision: "any problems with your eyesight, your vision?" Patient: "no" and "any difficulty with seeing bright lights?" Patient: "No"; Rash: "have you noticed any funny rashes at all, on your skin?" Patient: "no, no."

No past medical history: "are you otherwise fit and well? Or do you have any other medical problems I should be aware of?" Patient: "otherwise... I'm fine. There isn't anything that I'm taking or, I'm being treated for."
Use of paracetamol: "I've been taking some Paracetamol and Ibuprofen for that, and they help." This implies as-needed use for fever/symptoms.
Use of ibuprofen: same statement: "I've been taking some Paracetamol and Ibuprofen for that, and they help."
No known drug allergies: "any allergies at all to any medications, I should be aware of?" Patient: "no."
Grandmother with type 2 diabetes: "yeah my grandma has diabetes" and when asked type: "I think it's type two."
Great-grandfather with eczema: "I think, one of my great grandads had an eczema."
Living situation and occupation: "I live alone." and later: "I'm an, I'm an accountant."

Occasional cigars and social alcohol: Smoking: "yeah occasionally, you know, cigars and things on company parties." Alcohol: "occasionally yeah I would have some. I'm not a very big drinker" and doctor reiterates "socially with work."

Assessment of viral URTI / early flu-like illness: "I think you probably have, you know a bit of a viral, what we say viral illness, maybe a viral upper respiratory tract infection, or maybe early signs of a flu."
Advised rest and 1–2 days off work: "things you can do to really help yourself, is get plenty of rest. I'd probably advise you taking a day or two off work if you can."
Encouraged hydration: "Making yourself, pushing fluids and make yourself well-hydrated."
Continue paracetamol and ibuprofen: "Continue with the regular Paracetamol, Ibuprofen." This is in context of managing fever/illness symptoms.

Follow-up instructions: routine and urgent: "if next week you're still not better, I'd like you to come back and see me" and earlier: "if you have a high fever, or your breathing is becoming a bit more labored, or chest pain, I'd like you to come back and see me much sooner, give me a call."
